{"id":7,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"capabilities":{"prompts":{},"tools":{}},"instructions":"Orb is a programming language. A program is a finite graph of states and events: written as .lolo text, held as .orb data, compiled to a full-stack app. You build by composing installed behaviors (atoms own their state machine; you override data, event names and config), not by writing every state machine from scratch.\nLoop: (1) `behaviors` with no scopes lists the installed packages and topics; list a topic, then `describe_behavior` and `read_behavior` the ones that fit. (2) Write the .lolo file, importing them with `uses`. `reference` is the language reference; `operators`, `patterns` and `complete` tell you what the language accepts. (3) `validate` until it reports 0 errors and 0 warnings; every finding carries a code, a path and a fix. (4) `play` events through the machine to check it does what was asked. (5) Run it with `npx -y @almadar/orb serve <file>`.","protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","serverInfo":{"name":"orb","version":"18.0.5"}}}
